subject: How is variance around density estimated?

messages.author: 92467f99580efdc0
messages.subject: How is variance around density estimated?
parts:
I have output from oSCR and Bayesian scr0 that return essentially the same parameter estimates on the same data set, which is great. However, the SE around oSCR density is much higher than the sd summarized from the posterior distribution. Is this normal? Thought it might have to do with the resolution of the discrete state-space, but apparently not. I know that estimated density is log-based, but I didn't think that SE would be that different from the MCMC sd. I re-read Sutherland et al. (2019) but didn't catch anything about variance estimation. I'm sure it's derived from the information matrix, but beyond that, I'm not sure where to go for more information.

Thanks in advance,

Brian
